author: Mark Martin FOR JACKSON NEWSPAPERS
title: FRIDAY NIGHT LIGHTS: Ravenswood heads to Poca tonight | Jackson Star and Herald - Ripley and Ravenswood | wvnews.com
text:
RAVENSWOOD, W.Va. (WV News) - An old football rivalry is renewed tonight for the Ravenswood Red Devils.
Matt Peery's crew will be at O.O. White Stadium to face off with Poca for the first time since 2011.
Ravenswood enters at 0-2, having lost to St. Marys (13-0) in the opener and Ripley (49-0) last week.
Poca is 1-1 following a defeat of Buffalo (34-6) in Week 1 before falling hard to Midland Trail (55-0) in Week 2.
"Poca has some game-changing athletes at quarterback, running back and on the perimeter," said Devil head coach Matt Peery. "The quarterback (Kamauri McBride) has as live of an arm as we have seen all year. He can spin the ball. Our defensive backs have to be on their game and get to their coverage drops this week for us to be successful. No. 2 (Jackson McClanahan) is a freak athlete.
"No. 40 comes into the wildcat role and runs the ball really hard. We have to be sure tacklers at all times. Defensively, another odd front will test our offensive line. Ripley gave us fits with a 3-man front so that is our focus this week. We must do a better job physically up front and communicating. Ralphie Rhodes and Brandow Crow will be counted on to carry the ball a lot this week with Jakob Simmons being out with a head injury."
RED DEVIL FOOTBALL NOTES - Ravenswood leads the series, 15-13-1...The Devils have won the last four meetings...The two programs first met in 1935...Four of the games played were in the postseason with Poca holding a 3-1 edge...Poca is guided by Seth Ramsey, a Clay County native who is in his 11th season at the helm of the Dots...Ravenswood aims to end an 18-game losing streak tonight dating back to the 2023 season...Ramsey knows all about losing skids...He helped pull the proud Dot program out of the doldrums by snapping a 39-game losing streak in 2017...Poca has since enjoyed three playoff seasons, including a semifinal appearance in 2021...Poca has five state titles in program history to four for Ravenswood...Tonight's game airs on WMOV-FM (93.5 & 106.9), WMOV-AM (1360) and the WMOV on the Go App. Tom Hunter will be on the call.
